title: The Baker's Yeast Reference Genome: R64-1-1 (S288C)
description: The Baker's Yeast reference genome (Saccharomyces cerevisiae, assembly R64-1-1 (S288C)) spans approximately 12.16 Mb across 16 chromosomes, encoding approx 6,000 protein-coding genes (estimate). This record is the assembly-level overview: the anchor for the deterministic scale chromosome -> gene -> protein product -> pathway -> trait used across this database. REFERENCE GENOME ONLY: a public consensus assembly, never any real person's private genetic data.
how_it_works: Genome assembly stitches long sequencing reads into chromosome-scale scaffolds, annotates genes by homology and experiment, and publishes the consensus coordinates everyone references. All records in this database hang off these coordinates deterministically.
key_points: Assembly R64-1-1 (S288C): the public reference coordinates.
Size approximately 12.16 Mb; 16.
Gene content: approx 6,000 protein-coding genes (estimate).
standards: Coordinates follow the named assembly R64-1-1 (S288C)
Numeric values are approximate unless stated; estimates are labeled

demo.note: Prints the deterministic scale ladder for this genome.

provenance: JAH Databases genome lane (r18); public reference assembly facts; nucleotide examples are synthetic representative motifs, never real reference sequence and never any individual genome.

title: Baker's Yeast: The Deterministic Scale Ladder
description: The Deterministic Scale Ladder (Baker's Yeast). chromosome -> gene -> protein product -> pathway -> trait: each level is a deterministic function of the level below in the reference assembly. No level is a sample or a guess; the ladder is the database's spine.
how_it_works: Scaling walks the ladder deterministically: pick a level, apply its rules, land on the next level. The generator ladder ranks are simple -> most competitive -> mix-and-match -> unmade -> top-notch -> future grade -> god mode.
key_points: Deterministic: same level, same rules, same result.
Generator bound: stops at 10^15 records or complete-with-reason.
standards: Scaling claims are structural, not empirical, and labeled as such
citations: JAH Databases genome lane design notes
